title: Auto-Dig request #1902 Stewart's proposal pass
summary: Queue-first request pass reuses the two existing Stewart's targets and records the five-site and Hudson proposal rejection evidence without promoting proposed private sites to deployments.

sources.title: Residents question proposal for automatic license plate reader at Poestenkill intersection
Town of Poestenkill, Stewart's Shops oppose license plate readers from the county sheriff's department

data.research_question: What portion of request #1902 can be advanced now without duplicating existing Stewart's target identities?
data.method: Read the request and comments, reused the two existing canonical targets, and reconciled November-December 2025 reporting on the five Rensselaer proposals, the Hudson proposal, and Stewart's rejection rationale.
classification_rules: Reuse stable canonical IDs when materially equivalent targets already exist.
A rejected private-property proposal is not an active deployment.
Hosting, ownership, maintenance, administration, and query access remain separate until native terms establish them.

findings.finding: Two existing canonical Stewart's targets already cover the five Rensselaer sites and Hudson proposal and were reused.
Stewart's declined both the five-store Rensselaer proposal and a separate Hudson Police proposal.
Customer privacy resistance and discomfort with private-company hosting were publicly identified as parts of the rejection rationale.
